spec_case: PR #480 review findings F1-F4 on issue #479's own translation-layer list: character-class ranges (`[a-z]`, `[^0-9]`), a negated shortcut inside a class (`[\W]`), IGNORECASE combined with ASCII, and Python's 3.7+ must-advance scan rule (`^|\w+`)
description: Each of these broke an ordinary pattern before the fix: a class range like [a-z] matched only its two endpoints and a literal hyphen; [\W] behaved like \w (missing negation); IGNORECASE+ASCII together dropped case-insensitivity entirely; and a non-empty match immediately after an empty one (CPython's own documented example, re.findall(r'^|\w+', 'two words') == ['', 'two', 'words']) was skipped instead of reported.
